name: Direct Recode
description: Questions measure the same construct with compatible response formats. High-quality bridge variable; harmonization requires only deterministic recoding, category collapsing, or unit conversion.

name: Statistical Adjustment
description: Questions measure the same underlying construct but differ in measurement (reference period, response scale, or level of detail). Usable bridge variable with known limitations; requires a documented statistical transformation with stated assumptions.

name: Incompatible
description: Questions measure fundamentally different constructs or have barriers that no statistical method can bridge. Not a bridge variable; the barrier code explains the specific obstacle.

name: Construct
description: Construct/Concept differences. Questions measure different things. Most fundamental barrier; dominant category in the data. (Wolf 2016: concept differences; Fortier 2011: inferential equivalence)

name: Temporal
description: Reference period / temporal differences (e.g. hours worked last week vs. usual hours per year). (Wolf 2016: reference period differences; Fortier 2011: reference period)

name: Response Scale
description: Response scale / format differences (e.g. open dollar amount vs. bracketed income categories). (Saris & Gallhofer 2014)

name: Population/Coverage
description: Population or coverage differences (e.g. adults 18+ vs. persons 15+). (Slomczynski & Tomescu-Dubrow 2018: sampling design)

name: Mode/Context
description: Mode of administration or questionnaire context differences (e.g. self-administered web vs. interviewer telephone). (Wolf 2016: questionnaire context)

name: Processing/Metadata
description: Processing or metadata differences (e.g. SOC 2010 codes vs. SOC 2018 without crosswalk). Technical rather than conceptual. (Oleksiyenko 2018)
